Important flags and behaviors from the code:

- [.txt|--help.] / [.txt|-h.]
- [.txt|--list.] / [.txt|-l.]
- [.txt|--matchAny.] / [.txt|-m.]
- [.txt|--matchAll.] / [.txt|-M.]
- [.txt|--plainText.] / [.txt|-p.]

- [.txt|--showSkippedTests.] / [.txt|-s.]

- [.txt|--treeLevel.]
- [.txt|--debugger.] / [.txt|-D.]
- [.txt|--debugId.]

Important caveats visible in [.txt|mRunTests.cs.]:

- [.txt|--matchAll.] and [.txt|--matchAny.] must be the last flag pair because they consume every remaining argument as filter text
- the short flags for depth and debug id are distinct:
  [.txt|-d.] is [.txt|--treeLevel.], [.txt|-i.] is [.txt|--debugId.]
- [.txt|--plainText.] is also forced automatically when stdout is redirected
- the code also accepts numeric aliases such as [.txt|-1.], [.txt|-2.], ... for stopping after a limited number of failures, but for documentation and scripts the long [.txt|--stopOnFirstFail.] form is clearer
- the numeric aliases are not perfectly regular: [.txt|-8.] currently maps to [.txt|7.] and [.txt|-9.] to [.txt|8.], so they are best treated as legacy shortcuts
- the file-driven regression suite is current-working-directory-sensitive because [.txt|mRegression_Tests.] resolves [.txt|Regression.Tests/.] from [.txt|mFS.CWD().]

The test host starts the root group [.txt|All.], which is assembled in [.txt|SPO_CS/src/mRunTests.cs.] from [.txt|mCommon_Tests.Tests.] and [.txt|mSPO_Tests.Tests.].

That means the architecture is secured not only by unit tests, but also by complete file-driven runs.

[==Regression Harness==]

[.txt|mRegression_Tests.] reads, for each case under [.txt|SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/.]:

- [.txt|Name.SPO.]
- [.txt|Name.result.SPO.]
- [.txt|Name.ILT.]

Each case produces exactly three checks:

o 1. [.txt|.SPO == .result.SPO.]
o 2. [.txt|.SPO -> .ILT.]
o 3. [.txt|.ILT == .result.SPO.]

This tests three distinct contracts:

- direct SPO interpretation is semantically correct
- lowering to IL is stable
- IL execution is semantically equivalent to SPO execution

Important execution details from the code:

- the [.txt|.SPO.] file under test and the [.txt|.ILT.] file both run with [.txt|Module_Std.] as import
- the oracle file [.txt|.result.SPO.] runs with an empty import and must carry its expected semantics itself
- discovery uses [.txt|mFS.CWD() / "Regression.Tests".], so [.txt|mRunTests.] has to be launched from [.txt|SPO_CS/.] for this suite to appear at all
- only files whose names literally end in [.txt|.SPO.] are discovered as regression sources, so sibling scratch files such as [.txt|07_13_HigherOrderFuncTypes.SPO_Fail.] are not part of the harness
- files named [.txt|_*.SPO.] are intentionally skipped by the harness
- when the folder is missing, the current warning is low-signal:
  [.txt|Folder not found: mFS+tFolder.]

If the generated IL text differs from the stored [.txt|.ILT.], the harness writes [.txt|Name.ILT.new.].

As checked on [.txt|2026-04-22.], that folder currently yields [.txt|49.] discovered regression source files, which means [.txt|147.] file-driven regression checks before the rest of the unit and module suites are counted.

[==Why This Test Structure Is Architecturally Strong==]

It covers exactly the places where this repository is most likely to drift:

- text syntax
- desugaring
- type analysis
- lowering
- IL stability
- VM execution
- module initialization
